purpose: Problem-first context for mapping a user request to a formal graph problem, a validated GraphMine operation, a backend, parameters, and optional outputs.

source_of_truth.problem_contracts: Each problems/*/problem.json object is embedded exactly and remains authoritative for semantics, inputs, outputs, validation rules, and edge cases.

scope.operation_count_note: Triangle counting and dynamic triangle counting share one research problem but are separate runnable operations.

routing.model_policy: Supply this catalog to the base router. The frozen legacy routing adapter was evaluated on the earlier 20-problem contract; do not silently extend its evaluation claims.

workflow.instruction: Compare the user request with problem_statement, intent_signals, graph_input, problem_inputs, solution_semantics, and edge_cases. Select exactly one problem_id or report ambiguity.
Inspect library_support. If status is no_validated_backend, report that faithfully and do not substitute a nearby problem.
Choose among library_support.operation_ids. Respect each operation's validated_profile and backend_constraints; these can be narrower than the general problem contract.
Use spec.graph_input and spec.problem_inputs for semantic requirements, then use operation.cli for their concrete command-line encoding. Ask for any required graph or auxiliary input that is missing.

Honor an explicit supported backend choice. Otherwise use auto or choose from backend_details only when capabilities, constraints, or available hardware justify it. Never silently replace an explicitly selected backend.
Always return required_outputs. Enable optional fields only through operation.cli.optional_output_flags when the user requests them or they are necessary for the task.

hard_rules: Do not route an unsupported problem to a superficially similar supported operation.
Do not claim support outside an operation's validated_profile or backend_constraints.
Do not invent parameter values for required inputs; request them from the user.
Use canonical external vertex and edge IDs at the public boundary.
Prefer the generic run/supports/result lifecycle; use problem-specific fields only where the contract requires them.

disambiguation.rule: Maximal means enumerate inclusion-maximal cliques; maximum means find a largest clique.
Use densest_k_subgraph only when the vertex cardinality k is fixed.
Triangles are a fixed 3-cycle query; motifs count supplied small patterns; graphlets request a graphlet/orbit census; subgraph isomorphism matches a specific query graph and its embeddings.
Use community_detection for one assignment per vertex and overlapping community detection when vertices may belong to several communities.
Use temporal motifs when edge-event order or a time window is part of the query.

build_once_run_many.execution_model: Compile and link the validated implementations once. Each later query invokes the same binary with an operation, backend, canonical graph JSON, parameters, and optional-output flags.
why: No C++ or CUDA compilation occurs per user query.
The command boundary is stable JSON input and JSON output.
The runtime list command reports which validated backends were compiled into the current binary.
A long-lived service can invoke this binary now and can later call the same C++ library in-process if process startup becomes material.

options.description: CUDA device IDs; current validated paths use the first ID unless their facade states otherwise.
Explicitly permit an undirected projection for an undirected operation.

spec.name: Signed Network Structural Balance and Frustration Minimization
spec.problem_statement: Given a graph whose edges are each labeled positive or negative, determine whether it is structurally balanced (partitionable into two factions so every positive edge stays within a faction and every negative edge crosses factions), and when it is not, find a two-faction assignment minimizing the total weight of frustrated edges.

normalization: Every edge's type field must be exactly 'positive' or 'negative'; reject edges with any other or missing type.
Remove self-loops; a self-loop cannot be frustrated or unfrustrated under this definition.
Collapse parallel edges between the same pair only when they agree in sign; reject contradictory parallel signed edges between the same pair unless an explicit resolution policy is supplied.

problem_inputs.name: task
problem_inputs.description: Test exact structural balance via the cycle-based criterion, or find a minimum-frustration two-faction assignment.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Count frustrated edges or sum their declared nonnegative weights.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: balance_check is always solved exactly in linear time; frustration_minimization is NP-hard in general and approximate mode must disclose a bound.

required_outputs.name: balanced
required_outputs.description: Whether the graph is structurally balanced, i.e. the minimum achievable frustrated weight is zero.

required_outputs.name: faction_assignment
required_outputs.description: Two-faction partition of every vertex realizing the reported frustrated_weight.

required_outputs.name: frustrated_weight
required_outputs.description: Total weight (or count, under weight_mode=unweighted) of frustrated edges under faction_assignment: positive edges crossing factions plus negative edges within a faction.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether global optimality was proven for the requested task.

optional_outputs.name: frustrated_edges
optional_outputs.description: Edges violating faction_assignment under the sign rule.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified bound or gap-to-best-known for an approximate frustration_minimization result.

solution_semantics.objective: Find faction_assignment minimizing frustrated_weight, where a positive edge is frustrated if its endpoints are in different factions and a negative edge is frustrated if its endpoints are in the same faction; balanced=true exactly when the achieved minimum frustrated_weight is zero.
solution_semantics.exactness: balance_check always returns optimal=true via the linear-time cycle-based (parity-propagation) test; frustration_minimization is NP-hard in general, so approximate mode must disclose approximation_bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each vertex is assigned to exactly one of the two factions (A or B).
solution_semantics.ordering: faction_assignment is an unordered partition; the A/B labels are arbitrary beyond grouping and may be swapped per connected component.

validation_rules: Every edge's type in the normalized graph is exactly 'positive' or 'negative'.
frustrated_weight recomputes exactly from faction_assignment, edge signs, and (if weight_mode=edge_weight) edge weights.
balanced=true is independently verifiable via the standard cycle criterion: every cycle has an even number of negative edges.
balance_check always returns optimal=true.
edge_cases: An all-positive graph is trivially balanced by placing each connected component entirely in one faction.
A single negative edge between two otherwise-isolated vertices is trivially balanced by placing its endpoints in different factions.
Disconnected graphs: each connected component's faction assignment, and which label is 'A' vs 'B', is independent of other components.
A graph containing an odd negative cycle cannot be balanced; frustration_minimization must still return a feasible assignment with frustrated_weight > 0.

validation_rules: Every randomized sample underlying null_distribution_summary satisfies null_model's declared invariant exactly (e.g. an identical degree sequence, vertex count, and edge count to the input graph for degree_preserving_configuration).
z_score recomputes exactly from observed_value and null_distribution_summary's mean and standard deviation.
empirical_p_value recomputes exactly as the fraction of null_distribution_samples at least as extreme as observed_value, when samples are returned.
complete=true only when all sample_count randomizations succeeded and were evaluated.
edge_cases: A graph whose degree sequence admits only one simple realization yields a null distribution with zero variance; z_score is reported as null rather than divided by zero.
sample_count=1 yields a valid but very high-variance estimate of the null distribution.
A statistic_definition invariant under the chosen null_model by construction (e.g. vertex count) trivially yields z_score zero.
Isolated (zero-degree) vertices remain isolated in every randomized sample under degree_preserving_configuration.
